channel.title: Lynn Group Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Lynn Group Media (hoganstand.com)

item.title: GAA on TV: provincial final action takes centre stage
item.description: The Ulster and Munster club SHC finals along with the Connacht club SFC final will be shown live on TV this weekend.

item.title: Niamh McIntosh on captaining Moneyglass to a first Ulster title and, honoring her mother
item.description: Considering how strongly connected her family is to the club, Niamh McIntosh has felt privileged to be captain of St Ergnat's Moneyglass for their successful 2025 championship campaign.

item.title: Kilbrittain see off Kilrossanty for Munster club JHC glory
item.description: Kilbrittain (Cork) landed the Munster club junior hurling championship title by brushing aside Kilrossanty (Waterford) with a 2-17 to 0-9 victory in Mallow this afternoon.

item.title: Kiltimagh triumph over Aghavas to Connacht club JFC crown
item.description: Kiltimagh (Mayo) are Connacht club junior football champions after a double score win over Aghavas (Letrim) in Carrick-on-Shannon this afternoon.

item.title: Inter-county players to own image rights after GAA and GPA agree new recognition protocol
item.description: The GAA and GPA are pleased to announce that a new Recognition Protocol to cover the next four years (2026 to 2029) has been agreed between the two associations. The agreement follows a lengthy period of negotiations after the last arrangement was initially extended by one year.

item.title: Upperchurch-Drombane sink 12-man O'Callaghan's Mills in second-half to claim Munster title
item.description: Upperchurch-Drombane (Tipperary) produced the goods in the second-half to defeat 12-man O'Callaghan's Mills (Clare) by 3-20 to 0-15 at TUS Gaelic Grounds this evening to capture the Munster club intermediate hurling championship title.

item.title: Camogie: Barrs and Athenry come out on top in thrillers to reach All-Ireland club senior final
item.description: Two thrilling semi-finals saw Athenry (Galway) and St Finbarr's (Cork) secure their passage through to the AIB All-Ireland senior club camogie final at Croke Park in a fortnight, with Athenry edging out Dicksboro in a defensive battle at Kinnegad while Ciara Golden etched her name into the history of the famous Leeside club with the winning score against Loughgiel Shamrocks at the end of extra, extra time in Donoughmore-Ashbourne.

item.title: Athy and 'Boden set for Leinster club SFC final showdown
item.description: Athy will play Ballyboden St Enda's in the Leinster club senior football championship final after both sides recorded comfortable victories in their respective semi-finals this afternoon.

item.title: Slaughtneil keep it to script against St John's to retain Ulster club SHC title
item.description: Slaughtneil made it back-to-back Ulster club senior hurling championship titles thanks to a comprehensive 0-23 to 0-10 victory against St John's at the Box-It Athletic Grounds this evening.
